text:
maria: FYI ran nsys on the latest CI image; most CUDA kernels show up as <unknown> and host stacks are missing line info. Perf regression visible in telemetry. anyone seen this recently?

tim: Which nsys command did you run? image name? driver versions?

maria: Command: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=ci_trace ./bin/server --config /etc/serv/conf```
Image: redwood/runtime:ci-2026-03-01
Host driver: 535.54, container CUDA toolkit: 11.8 (from image).

raj: mismatch between host driver and container toolkit can bitrot CUPTI symbolic info. Also check that the image actually contains CUPTI libs under /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64. If CUPTI not present, nsys can't resolve many host/kern symbols.

maria: confirmed image doesn't have /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI. Who built the CI image?

devops: I updated base image to slim cuda-toolkit to cut size, might have dropped extras. Was told toolchain works for runtime, didn't test profiling.

perf-bot: automated profile saved: /artifacts/ci_trace.qdrep (size 42MB) :eyes:

tim: Two quick fixes to try: 1) mount host CUPTI into container at run time, 2) rebuild image with CUPTI installed and add debug flags during dev builds.

raj: Also ensure binaries have line info. For nvcc/host build use: ```-g -lineinfo -Xcompiler "-rdynamic -g"``` and for gcc builds avoid stripping. If you run a release image with `strip` or `-s` we won't get symbols.

maria: ah we do run `strip` in the final multi-stage image. For tracing I was profiling the slim release image. No wonder.

tim: For a quick repro without rebuilding: run container with host CUPTI mounted: ```docker run --gpus all --rm -v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH redwood/runtime:ci-2026-03-01 bash -c "nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=/tmp/trace ./bin/server"```
Then open with: ```nsys-ui /tmp/trace.qdrep```

raj: Also set these env vars so nsys picks up cupi: ```export CUPTI_LIB=/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64``` and ensure driver-toolkit compatibility. If you see kernel names but no source lines, you'll need the -lineinfo on the PTX/CU files.

maria: after mounting CUPTI I get kernel names back but still no host-line mappings for some inlined templated functions. stack shows libserver.so+0x3b4a instead of function::call_site.

tim: That usually means the binary lacks dynamic symbol table or got optimized/inlined. Build the debug variant with `-O0 -g` for repro OR at least keep symbols with `-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer` and avoid `-fdata-sections`/`-ffunction-sections` + aggressive LTO in the debug image.

devops: noted. For CI profiling we can switch to a `runtime:ci-debug` image that keeps symbols and includes CUPTI. I'll add a pipeline step to publish dev trace images.

raj: One more gotcha: CUPTI and Nsight require matching major.minor toolkit version (e.g., CUPTI from 11.8 with driver that supports 11.x). If you mix a 12.x driver with 11.8 CUPTI you can see truncated symbol mapping. Check `nvidia-smi` vs `/usr/local/cuda/version.txt`.

maria: stack sample from nsys: ```Host callstack: libserver.so (+0x3b4a) -> libtorch_cpu.so (+0x9e7f) -> libc.so.6(+0x46210)```
I rebuilt a dev image with -g and CUPTI mounted; now I see: ```Host callstack: MyModel::forward() at model.cpp:214 -> Inference::dispatch() at infer.cpp:88```

tim: Great — that confirms two issues: 1) stripped release image (no host symbols), 2) missing CUPTI in container (no kernel symbol mapping).

maria: Question: Should we keep symbols in dedicated perf images only, or carry them in all dev builds? Thoughts?

raj: Keep them out of production images for size/security. Add a small `runtime:profiling` tag with CUPTI and symbols enabled. Use it for perf runs and rollups. Also document required nvcc flags in BUILD.md.

devops: I'll create `runtime:profiling` and put instructions in the CI job `perf/profile` to use that tag. Also will add an automated smoke nsys run in nightly to catch regressions earlier.

perf-bot: perf job scheduled nightly at 04:00 UTC. Alerts will post to #eng-runtime/perf if tokenized latency changes > 10%. :robot_face:

maria: one last note — if you still see kernel names like `cuLaunchKernel_<hex>` that's JIT/PTX related; use `-Xptxas -v` and compile with `-lineinfo` to get richer kernel names and line mapping.

tim: Good call. I'll update the buildkite job to add `-lineinfo` for CUDA codepaths in the profiling image and add `--capture-range=nvtx` spans in our test harness so nsys only records the region we care about.

maria: thanks all, I'll re-run the failing benchmark with the new profiling image and paste the qdrep if anything looks off. :thumbsup:
